title: Commercial Real Estate Megatrend Resilience Index 2026
gist: Oxford Economics' 2026 index ranks 91 cities on CRE resilience to technology, demographic, climate and geopolitical megatrends: European cities lead, US tech hubs trade technology strength for climate/geopolitical weakness, and industrial is the most resilient sector while hotels are the least.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics' Global Megatrend Resilience Index for commercial real estate scores 91 cities in 33 countries, covering 97% of the global investible CRE universe.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Defines the breadth of the benchmark, so rankings are broadly representative of institutional CRE.
insights.locator: Our latest Global Megatrend Resilience Index

insights.claim: The index is forward-looking: four megatrend pillars (demographics, technology, geopolitics, climate) each combine six to ten indicators from long-range forecasts into pillar scores, which are weighted into an overall score out of 100.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Gives a structured lens for stress-testing CRE allocations against structural change rather than the cycle.
insights.quote: forward-looking index that tracks key CRE demand drivers across four key megatrends

insights.claim: Scores are produced per city at the all-property level and for five sectors (office, retail, industrial, residential, hotel), allowing city-by-sector comparison.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Enables sector-by-market selection rather than a single city or sector call.
insights.locator: Scores are calculated for each city

themes.theme: City rankings: Europe leads, US tech hubs and APAC mixed

insights.claim: European cities dominate CRE megatrend resilience, with Dublin, Oslo, Zurich, Stockholm and London leading by scoring well across technology, demographics, climate and geopolitics.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Suggests a structural case for European CRE exposure on long-term resilience grounds.
insights.quote: European cities dominate CRE megatrend resilience.

insights.claim: US technology hubs San Jose, Seattle and San Francisco top the technology pillar, but weaker climate and geopolitical resilience drag down their overall positions, creating a resilience trade-off.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Tech-driven demand in US hubs carries offsetting climate and geopolitical risk that may not be priced.
insights.quote: US technology hubs face a resilience trade-off.

insights.claim: Tokyo is the only Asia-Pacific city in the top ten, with Singapore 11th; Australian cities score well on demographics but climate risks hold back their overall rankings.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Asia-Pacific resilience is uneven, so selection matters more than regional exposure.
insights.quote: Tokyo is the only Asia-Pacific city in the top ten

insights.claim: Across the 91 cities, industrial is the most resilient CRE sector, followed by residential, retail and office, with hotels the least resilient.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Supports an overweight to industrial and residential and caution on hotels and office on structural grounds.
insights.quote: Industrial is the most resilient property sector.

insights.claim: Office ranks second-lowest and hotels last in megatrend resilience, implying these sectors are most exposed to technological, demographic, climate and geopolitical change.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Structural headwinds may justify a higher risk premium for office and hotel assets.
